purpose: Teach: 粉末/芳香/ソーラー/バカンス/渓谷/チャーハン/半袖/しょうゆ

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、お祖母ちゃんが粉末のお茶をくれたわ
lines.en: Sho, Grandma gave us some powdered matcha tea.
lines.style: Warm, matter-of-fact delivery. Slight lift of recognition that this is something to share with him. Gentle pace, unhurried. The tone of a mother offering something small but intentional.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、ぼく、お庭のお花の芳香が大好きだよ
lines.en: Mom, I really love the way the flowers smell in the garden.
lines.style: Bright, earnest observation. Opens with quiet wonder. Soft emphasis on 'smell'—he's noticing something adults miss. Small voice, genuine delight, not performing.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、お父さんが屋根にソーラーパネル付けたいって
lines.en: Sho, your dad was saying he wants to put solar panels on the roof.
lines.style: Casual, informational tone. Brief pause before the main idea, like she's deciding whether to mention it. Light, conversational—not heavy. Inviting his thoughts without prompting.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、ぼく、家族でバカンス行きたいよ
lines.en: Mom, I want to go on a family vacation.
lines.style: Hopeful, direct want. Open-hearted, without wheedling. Small but clear voice. A genuine wish expressed simply. Waiting to see if this might be possible.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、お父さんと渓谷温泉旅行に行きましょうね
lines.en: Sho, let's go on that hot spring trip to the valley with your dad, shall we?
lines.style: Tender offer, soft opener. Gently inclusive—'let's' and 'shall we' drawn slightly longer, inviting him in. Warm certainty underlying the question. A mother making something real.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、ぼく、お父さんが作るチャーハン上手だよ
lines.en: Mom, Dad's really good at making fried rice.
lines.style: Unguarded praise. Small pride in his voice—he's noticing something good about his dad and wants to say it. Quiet, genuine, no performance. Slight warmth on 'really good.'

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 翔くん、夏は半袖シャツに着替えましょうね
lines.en: Sho, when summer comes around, we should change you into short-sleeves, alright?
lines.style: Practical, gentle direction. Matter-of-fact but warm. No urgency—she's simply planting the idea. A mother's steady competence. Light touch on 'short-sleeves,' like it's obvious but worth saying.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: ママ、ぼく、おにぎりにしょうゆ少しつけて欲しい
lines.en: Mom, can you put just a little bit of soy sauce on my rice ball?
lines.style: Polite, specific request. Quiet emphasis on 'a little'—he's being precise about what he wants, not demanding. Open, trusting. The tone of a child comfortable asking for small things.
